questions.question:
**In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the "No error" option.**

The former first lady designed (1)/ it herself as a weekend (2)/ retreat away from White House. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution: ‘Retreat’ means to go back or withdraw, which is completely irrelevant in the given sentence. ‘Retreat’ must be replaced by ‘treat’ means ‘a celebration’ or ‘a gift’. The former first lady designed must have designed something as a ‘celebration’ away from (not at) White House. Since the error lies in the third part of the sentence, option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the "No error" option.**

Traditionally, fuel prices were determined (1)/ on a cost-plus basis, which led domestic prices (2)/ to fall at line with the cost of inputs like crude oil. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution: ‘To fall in line’ is a phrase which means to agree with others. Thus, in the third part of the sentence, the preposition ‘at’ must be replaced by ‘in’ to make the sentence grammatically correct.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent sentence.**

The next morning

P: it was snowing

Q: we woke up

R: and found that
questions.solution: R cannot be the first or the last part as it begins with the conjunction ‘and’ and ends with ‘that’. It has to be the second part. Thus, options 3 and 4 are incorrect. You will get up first and then find that it is snowing and not the other way round. Thus Q should be the first part. Hence the correct sequence is QRP.

questions.question: In a row of 40 students, A is 13th from left end. What is his place from the right end?
questions.solution:
Total students = 40

A’s position form left = 13

Total students = Position of student from right side + Position from left - 1

Position of student from right side = Total students - Position from left + 1

A’s position form right = 40 – 13 + 1

→ 40 – 12 = 28

Hence, A is 28th form right.

questions.question: If the ratio of the present ages of P and Q is 3 : 5 and the sum of their ages 4 years ago was 64, then what was the ratio of their ages 4 years ago?
questions.solution:
The ratio of the present ages of P and Q = 3 : 5

Let P’s present age be 3x and Q’s present age be 5x

The sum of their present ages = 64 (sum of ages 4 years ago) + 8

3x + 5x = 72 years

8x = 72 → x = 9

The present age of P = 3x → 3 × 9 → 27 years

The present age of Q = 5x → 5 × 9 → 45 years

The ratio of their ages 4 years ago = (27 – 4)/(45 – 4)

→ 23/41

Hence, the ratio of ages of P and Q, 4 years ago, is ’23 : 41’.

questions.question: What is the value of (√5 + 2)/ (√5 - 2)?
What is the value of 31 + 32 + ….. 50?
questions.solution:
Let’s consider the series as a geometric progression:

⇒ First term = a = 31; common difference = d = 1

⇒ last term = An = 50

We know, Sum of an AP = n/2 [a + An] (1)

Finding n: 

⇒ An = a + (n - 1)d

⇒ 50 = 31 + nd - 1 = 30 + n

∴ n = 50 - 30 = 20

⇒ Sum = 20/2 [31 + 50] = 10×81 = 810

∴ Sum of the series = 810

questions.question: Which of the following is greatest number?
Two pipes P and Q can fill the tank alone in 60 and 90 hours respectively. If they are opened together, then in how many hours will the tank be filled?
questions.solution:
Part of tank filled by P in 1 hour = 1/60

Part of tank filled by Q in 1 hour = 1/90

⇒ Part of tank filled by both in 1 hour = 1/60 + 1/90 = (3 + 2)/180 = 5/180

∴ Time taken by both to fill the tank = 180/5 = 36 hours

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 20 hours and pipe B can fill the same tank in 24 hours. Pipe C can empty the same tank in 12 hours. If all the pipes are opened together, then what portion of the tank will be filled after 12 hours?
questions.solution:
Part filled by A in 1 hour = 1/20

Part filled by B in 1 hour = 1/24

Part emptied by C in 1 hour = 1/12

∴ part filled when all are opened in 1 hour = 1/20 + 1/24 - 1/12 = (6 + 5 - 10)/120 = 1/120

∴ Portion of tank filled in 12 hours = 12 × (1/120) = 1/10

questions.question: What is the area (in cm²) of an equilateral triangle whose side is 16 cm?

**Given:**

Side of the equilateral triangle = 16 cm

questions.question: A shop - keeper offers 30% discount on bags which have been marked 60% above the cost price. Rahul bought the bag for Rs. 672. What was the cost price (in Rs) of the bag?
A merchant purchases a watch for Rs 540 and fixes its marked price in such a way that after allowing a discount of 10%, he earns a profit of 35%. What is the marked price (in Rs) of the watch?
questions.solution:
Let the MP = x

⇒ CP = 540 (Given)

SP = x - 0.1x = 0.9x

Profit = 35%

⇒ (SP - CP)/CP = 0.35

⇒ (0.9x - 540)/540 = 0.35

⇒ 0.9x - 540 = 189

⇒ 0.9x = 729

⇒ x = 729/0.9 = 810

∴ MP = Rs. 810

 

Alternative Method:

Relationship between CP and MP

CP : MP = (100 - D%) : (100 + P%)

CP : MP = (100 - 10) : (100 + 35) = 2 : 3

2 unit = 540

∴ 3 units = 810

questions.question: The ratio of two numbers is 7 : 12. If their difference is 60, then what is the smallest number?
questions.solution:
Let the numbers be 7x and 12x

12x - 7x = 60

⇒ 5x = 60

⇒ x = 60/5 = 12

∴ Smallest number = 7x = 7 × 12 = 84

questions.question: Rs. 2160 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5 respectively. What is the difference (in Rs.) between the shares of A and B?
questions.solution:
Let the shares of A, B and C be 2x, 3x and 5x

⇒ 2x + 3x + 5x = 2160

⇒ 10x = 2160 ⇒ x = 2160/10 = 216

⇒ A’s share = 216 × 2 = 432; B’s share = 3 × 216 = 648

∴ Difference of A’s and B’s shares = 648 - 432 = 216

questions.question: The average of 10 numbers is 9.5. If a number 5 is removed, then what will be the new average?
questions.solution:
Given: Average of 10 numbers = 9.5

⇒ (Sum of 10numbers)/10 = 9.5

⇒ Sum of 10 numbers = 95

New sum = Sum of 10 numbers - 5 = 95 - 5 = 90

∴ New average = 90/9 = 10

questions.question: An article is sold at a profit of 30%. If the selling price is doubled, then what will be the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Let the CP = x

⇒ SP = x + 0.3x = 1.3x

New SP = 2 × 1.3x = 2.6x

⇒ Profit = (2.6x - x)/x×100 = 160%

∴ Profit % = 160

questions.question: A man sold 400 chairs and had a gain equal to selling price of 50 chairs. What is his profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Let the SP of 1 chair = x

⇒ SP of 400 chairs = 400x

Given, Profit = 50x

⇒ CP = 400x - 50x = 350x

∴ Profit % = [(400x - 350x)/350x] ×100 = 14.28%

questions.question: 1000 is first increased by 10% and then it is decreased by 30%. What is the final value?
questions.solution:
Initial value = 1000

⇒ After increase of 10% = 1000 + 0.1 × 1000 = 1100

After decrease of 30%:

⇒ 1100 - 0.3 × 1100 = 1100 - 330 = 770

∴ Final value = 770

questions.question: Out of the total bags, 30% of bags are green coloured. 30% of remaining bags are red coloured. 40% of remaining bags are yellow coloured. The remaining 1176 bags are blue coloured. How many total bags are there?
questions.solution:
Let the total number of bags = x

Green coloured bags = 0.3x

⇒ Remaining bags = x - 0.3x = 0.7x

⇒ Red coloured bags = 0.3 × 0.7x = 0.21x

Remaining bags = 0.7x - 0.21x = 0.49x

Yellow coloured bags = 0.4 × 0.49x = 0.196x

⇒ Remaining bags = 0.49x - 0.196x = 0.294x

Given: 0.294x = 1176

⇒ x = 1176/0.294 = 4000

∴ Total no. of bags = 4000

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 8 km/hr. It covers a distance of 40 km upstream in 8 hours. What is the speed (in km/hr) of the stream?
questions.solution:
Let the speed of stream = a km/hr

⇒ Speed upstream = 8 - a km/hr

Distance = 40 km; Time = 8 hours

⇒ Speed = Distance/Time

⇒ 8 - a = 40/8 = 5

⇒ a = 8 - 5 = 3 km/hr

∴ Speed of stream = 3 km/hr

questions.question: A 400 metres long train crosses a bridge 600 metres long in 50 seconds. What is speed (in km/hr) of the train?
questions.solution:
Total distance covered = 400 + 600 = 1000 m

⇒ Speed = 1000/50 = 20 m/s

∴ Speed of train = 20 × (18/5) = 72 km/hr (∵ Multiplied by 18/5 to convert to km/hr)

questions.question: What is the difference between the number of students who play Tennis and those who play Polo?
questions.solution:
No. of students playing Tennis = 1080 × (108/360) = 324

No. of students playing Polo = 1080 × (36/360) = 108

questions.question: In which of the following group of sports, the sum of the number of students who play in the first 2 groups is equal to that of the third group?
questions.solution:
No. of students playing Tennis = 1080× (108/360) = 324

No. of students playing Polo = 1080× (36/360) = 108

No. of students playing Cricket = 1080× (72/360) = 216

No. of students playing Hockey = 1080× (90/360) = 270

No. of students playing Golf = 1080× (54/360) = 162

Checking each option one by one:

1: Cricket + Polo = 216 + 108 = 324 is not equal to hockey

2: Hockey + Tennis = 270 + 324 = 594 is not equal to Golf

3: Cricket + Polo = 216 + 108 = 324 = Tennis

4: Hockey + Cricket = 270 + 216 = 486 is not equal to Tennis

∴ Option 3 is correct.

questions.question: What is the total number of students who play either Hockey or Cricket?
questions.solution:
No. of students playing Cricket = 1080 × (72/360) = 216

No. of students playing Hockey = 1080 × (90/360) = 270

∴ Total no. of students who play either Hockey or Cricket = 270 + 216 = 486

questions.question: Every production is organised by combining land, labour, physical and human capital which are known as _________.
questions.solution:
• Each production is dependent on the combination of land, labour, physical and Human capital which are commonly known as **'Factors of Production'.**
 
• In order to carry out operations or production, we need **a land (a place**) to set up the production, **the labour** to carry out production, **Physical capital** for transport and for purchasing of goods and **human capital** to direct the labour to ease the production process.
 
• All the other things like organisations or Industries and economic activities are inter-connected and dependent on **factors of Production.**

questions.question: Market activities in an economy involve ________.

options.text: activities performed for Pay or Profit

questions.solution:
• Economic activities are basically defined as production, distribution and final consumption of the commodities by the consumer. Therefore, Market activities in Economy basicallyinvolve **activities performed for Pay or Profit**.

 
• Economic activities are basically of four types:
 
• **Primary Sector (Raw Materials)**
 
• **Secondary Sector (Industry and Manufacturing)**
 
• **Tertiary Sector (Service Sector)**
 
• **Quaternary Sector (Knowledge Sector)**

questions.question: Who among the following has the power to dissolve Lok Sabha?
questions.solution:
• According to **Article 85 (2)(b)** of the Constitution of India, **The President of India** has the ultimate power to dissolve the Lok Sabha.
 
• **The Lok Sabha has a term of five years**, but if the concerned authority wants, it can be dissolved earlier.
 
• There are two ways in which the Lok Sabha can be dissolved:
 
• Firstly, when the leader of the majority (the ruling party) dissolves the LokSabha.
 
• Secondly, when the leader of the single largest party doesn’t gain the majority in the Lok Sabha, then the entitled power passes the authority to the President.

questions.question: Part IV A of the Indian Constitution describes about_________.
questions.solution:
• **Fundamental Duties **are defined in Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Fundamental Duties are the moral obligations of all the citizens of India.
 
• There are 11 Fundamental duties.
 
• **Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by 42ⁿd Amendment of Constitution in the year 1976.**
 
• Fundamental Duties are non-justifiable and non-legally enforceable but it is expected from every citizen of country to promote and uphold the spirit of patriotism and unity in India.

questions.question: In Indus Valley Civilization, site ‘Dholavira’, has been located in which state of India?
questions.solution:
• ‘**Dholavira**’, commonly known as **Kotada**, is an archaeological site located in **Gujarat (Rann of Kutch District).**
 
• Dholavira was discovered by **J.P Joshi** in the year **1967. **
 
• Dholavira was an important centre of trade between **Gujarat, Sindh, Punjab and Western Asia. **

questions.question: In which year did Indian National Congress reunite after the famous ‘Surat split’?
questions.solution:
• The **reunion of the two wings **of the **Indian National Congress**took place in the year** 1916**, in the Lucknow session.
 
• The **Surat Split** (1907) is remarked as the division between the leaders of Indian National Congress (INC) which had two segregations of ideologies mainly by extremists and moderators, held at the Surat Session in the year 1907.
 
• The group of moderators dominated **the Indian National Congress** between the period of 1885-1905, whereas the other group of extremists remained outside and did not dominate the INC by not participating in the major activities.

questions.question: Our Solar system is a part of which galaxy?
questions.solution:
• Our Solar System is a part of the ‘**Milky Way’** galaxy.
 
• Milky Way galaxy is the huge crunch of stars which are congregated together in the Universe space.
 
• Milky Way galaxy is a barred spiral with four major arms in its **disk, one spur and outer arm. **It was formed around **12 billion years ago.**

questions.question: The ‘Alps Mountains’ are which type of mountains?
questions.solution:
• The Alps Mountains are ‘**Young Fold Mountains’.**
 
• The Alps Mountains are the **highest and most extensive** **mountain range in Europe** which were formed millions of years ago.
 
• The effects of folding on the layers within the upper part of the crust of Earth leads to the formation of the ‘fold mountains.

questions.question: Which of the following is produced from the Pancreas?
questions.solution:
• **‘Insulin’**is produced from the endocrine gland namely ‘**Pancreas**’.
 
• Insulin is a hormone secreted by the Pancreas (beta cells) that **helps the body to store and use the glucose.**
 
• Insulin helps to keep the blood sugar level in control, from getting too high or too low.
 
• Deficiency of ‘insulin’ leads to ‘**diabetes**’.

questions.question: Which part of the plant helps in holding the plant firmly in the soil?
questions.solution:
• **Roots of the plant** help in holding the plant firmly in the soil.
 
• Roots suck water and nutrients from the soil and transfer the same into the plants.
 
• Roots also help in holding the soil together.
 
• Roots are generally of two types- **Tap Roots and Fibrous Roots.​**

questions.question: Percentage of O₂ present in inhaled air in human is about ________.
questions.solution:
• Human Being inhales **21% of O₂ (Oxygen)** present in the air.
 
• **Nitrogen** makes to **78%**of the air which human breathes in, followed by 21% of Oxygen and **0.04%** of **Carbon dioxide**.
 
• Human Being breathes oxygen from their mouth into their lungs. The chest cavity containing the lungs expand and contract with the diaphragm as it moves down and up.

questions.question: The SI unit of Pressure is __________.
questions.solution:
• SI unit of pressure is **‘Pascal’ **and its formula sign is** Pa.**
 
• Pressure is defined as the force per unit area (pressure=force/area).
 
• 1 Pascal equals the pressure of **1 newton per square meter and the formula is as follows:**

**1 Pa= 1N / m² ≡ 1 kg / m.**

questions.question: The image formed by a plane mirror is ________.
questions.solution:
• The **image** formed by a **plane mirror** is always **virtual.**
 
• The image formed is ‘virtual’ because it is a copy of an object formed at the location from which the light rays appear to come.
 
• A plane mirror is a mirror with a **flat reflective surface**. For light rays striking a plane mirror, the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence. Therefore, the angle of reflection is the angle between the reflected ray and the normal.

questions.question: What are the two major file systems in Microsoft Windows?
questions.solution:
• There are two major file systems in Microsoft Windows, namely, **NTFS and FAT.**
 
• **FAT (File Allocation Table) **is generally supported by the Microsoft Windows OS and the system was inherited from old DOS.
 
• Whereas, **NTFS** is a file system that supports larger file sizes and hard drives. **NTFS is the default file system of the Windows NT family.**

questions.question: What is the Atomic Mass of Hydrogen?
questions.solution:
• The Atomic Mass is defined as the sum of the numbers of Neutrons and Protons in the nucleus of an atom and the **Atomic Mass of Hydrogen is 1 amu****.**
 
• **Hydrogen **has no neutrons in its nucleus.

 **Atomic Mass = Total No. of Protons + Total No. of Neutrons**
 
• Hydrogen is the **first element** of the periodic table.

questions.question: If the pH of a solution is 7, it is ________.
questions.solution:
• The **pH **value of a **‘neutral’ **solution is **7.** Generally, pH greater than 7 is considered basic and pH less than 7 is considered acidic.
 
• The **pH value** is defined as a measure of the molar concentration of hydrogen ions in a particular solution to measure the degree of the acid or base of the solution.
 
• For instance, **pure water** is neutral, at pH 7, which shows properties of neither being acidic in nature nor a base.

questions.question: Forests are examples of ________.
questions.solution:
• **Forests** are the example of **Natural Ecosystems. **
 
• Ecosystems comprise of **all living and non-living species** in a specific local environment.
 
• Natural ecosystem is the result of interactions between environment and organism.
 
• In a natural ecosystem, **sunlight** is the energy source of its plants and this energy drives all biological cycle.

questions.question: What is the tagline for ‘Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana’?
questions.solution:

• The policy was launched in the year **2015-2016** to promote farming and irrigation.
 
• The main objective of the scheme is to converge the investments in irrigation at the farm level and provide end to end solutions to the farmers.

questions.question: Sir C.V Raman is famous for ________.
questions.solution:

questions.question: The Amaravati School of Art developed under the patronage of the ‘Satavahanas’ of which region?
questions.solution:

• Amaravati School of Art is famously known for its ‘**stupas’,** which are distinctively made from white marble.

questions.question: MahaChakriSirindhorn has been conferred with first "World Sanskrit Award" belongs to which country?

questions.question: Which was an operation by Indian Armed forces to foil the coup in Maldives?
